claims.claim: Bulgaria has no wealth tax

sources.name: PwC: Bulgaria, individual, other taxes
sources.says: Last reviewed 02 August 2026. "There are no net wealth/worth taxes in Bulgaria." "The aggregate rate of health insurance contributions is 8%". "The minimum monthly insurance base for freelancers is EUR 550.66 from 1 January 2026 until 31 July." The page has no inheritance or gift tax section.

sources.name: PwC: quick chart, net wealth/worth tax rates
sources.says: Headline net wealth/worth tax rate: Greece "NA" (last reviewed 08 September 2026), Cyprus "NA" (04 August 2026), Croatia "NA" (27 August 2026), Bulgaria "NA" (02 August 2026). "NA" is defined as "Not Applicable (i.e. the territory does not have the indicated tax or requirement)".

claims.claim: Residents pay a 5% final tax on foreign dividends

sources.name: PwC: Bulgaria, individual, income determination
sources.says: Last reviewed 02 August 2026. "Dividends and liquidation proceeds paid by Bulgarian and foreign entities are subject to a 5% final WHT at source"; where a foreign payer does not withhold, "the tax is payable by the recipient themselves on an annual basis." "Interest income from bank accounts in the European Union / European Economic Area is tax free as of 1 April 2022"; other bank interest "is taxable at a tax rate of 10% as of 1 April 2022 instead of a final tax rate of 8%". Exempt: "Capital gains from transactions with securities of public companies on the Bulgarian Stock Exchange or on a regulated securities market in EU/EEA countries", extended from 1 January 2021 to "equivalent third-country stock markets as defined in EU Directives 2014/65/EU"; otherwise "Capital gains are taxed on an annual basis with a 10% flat tax rate".

claims.note: nra.bg was not searched for a page on this; PwC's page is dated August 2026. Plovdiv's `why` ("Bulgaria taxes dividends at 5%"), the tagline and the summary agree; scores.tax stays 4 (5% on dividends but 10% on US interest).

claims.claim: Bulgaria's municipal inheritance tax fully exempts children and grandchildren

sources.name: Innovires: inheritance tax in Bulgaria
sources.says: Published and last updated 10 April 2026. "the surviving spouse and direct line heirs (children, parents, grandchildren) are fully exempt from inheritance tax" (Art. 31(2) LTFA). Siblings and their children pay 0.4% to 0.8%, others 3.3% to 6.6%, above "EUR 127,823 (BGN 250,000) per heir". Bulgarian nationals are "taxed on the entire inheritance, including assets located abroad"; foreign nationals "only on property situated on the territory of the Republic of Bulgaria." It does not address foreign nationals who live in Bulgaria as a separate case.

sources.name: PwC: quick chart, inheritance and gift tax rates
sources.says: Greece (08 September 2026): inheritance "Category A: 10; Category B: 20; Category C: 40". Cyprus (04 August 2026): inheritance "NA"; gift "Nil if up to a third degree relative." Croatia (27 August 2026): "4" and "4". Bulgaria (02 August 2026): "Varies depending on category of the heir and the amount of the inheritance."; gift 3.3% to 6.6% to the municipalities.

claims.note: The statute could not be read: lex.bg returned HTTP 403 (https://lex.bg/laws/ldoc/2134174720, the Local Taxes and Fees Act), and PwC's Bulgaria page has no inheritance section. A law-firm page dated April 2026 was used, as the profile already says. Plovdiv's `why` ("children inherit free") agrees. localTaxes.ts agrees (BG has no inheritance entry and its note says the same).

sources.name: LYNX: Key Information Document (help page of a broker whose accounts are carried by Interactive Brokers)
sources.says: Retail clients are "not permitted to trade ETFs or other products that do not have a valid KID"; many non-EU ETFs have none. Can a retail client buy US ETFs? sources.says: Last updated 2 November 2026. "PRIIPs is an EU rule that prohibits buying US-listed ETFs", and this also applies to UK investors; US ETFs are open only to elective professional clients, while UCITS ETFs are available to all Europeans.

claims.claim: The block is on buying, not on holding US-listed ETFs

sources.name: LYNX: Key Information Document (help page of a broker whose accounts are carried by Interactive Brokers)
sources.says: The page's FAQ says retail clients "may still hold or sell existing positions, but new purchases are restricted."

sources.name: Regulation (EU) No 1286/2014, Article 13, as adopted (legislation.gov.uk copy of the EU text)
sources.says: The duty to provide a KID falls on "a person advising on, or selling, a PRIIP" before the retail investor is bound; nothing in the article reaches a PRIIP the investor already holds or a sale by the investor.

claims.claim: The route is a pensioner D visa, then a residence permit renewed for up to a year at a time, and it needs a right to a pension

sources.name: Innovires: type D visa for Bulgaria
sources.says: Published March 19, 2026; last updated October 8, 2026. Art. 24(1)(10): "Right to a pension under Bulgarian or foreign law and sufficient means of subsistence." Means of "not less than the Bulgarian minimum monthly wage (EUR 620.20 as at 2026)" (Art. 24(2)). A long-stay permit is issued for up to one year unless the law provides otherwise. Art. 24(1)(19): "At least BGN 600,000 (EUR 306,775.13) in Bulgarian real estate." Insurance with "cover of at least EUR 30,000 for repatriation, emergency care and hospital treatment". Every ground listed has its own requirement; none is savings alone.

claims.note: mfa.bg's D visa sheets are PDFs (https://www.mfa.bg/upload/99380/2_Visa_D.pdf, https://mfa.bg/upload/716/VISA_TYPE_D.pdf) and could not be read here; a law-firm page updated October 2026 was used. Summary, drawback 1 and Plovdiv's `why` ("residence needs a pension") agree; scores.visa stays 3 (a pension requirement).
